clippings.speaker: Joel Coen
clippings.quote: We’re lucky we found Roger. He understands what we are after, and frequently comes up with stuff on the spot that reflects what we want to do in the scene — but perhaps in a much better realization of it, given the setup.
clippings.title: Fargo: Cold-Blooded Scheming
clippings.context: Joel Coen on Deakins in American Cinematographer's 1996 Fargo production story, republished online by the ASC in 2020.

clippings.speaker: Joel Coen
clippings.quote: We always involve Roger very early. Basically, what we do after we finish the script is sit down with him and talk in general terms about how we were thinking about it from a visual point of view. … So he’s involved pretty much right from the beginning. The style of the shooting is worked out between the three of us.
clippings.title: Fargo: Cold-Blooded Scheming
clippings.context: Joel Coen describing how the brothers bring Deakins into pre-production and storyboarding.

clippings.speaker: Joel Coen
clippings.quote: He has been quietly bringing us around to longer lenses. It’s a joke between the three of us. We’re now up to 32mm and 35mm lenses!
clippings.title: Fargo: Cold-Blooded Scheming
clippings.context: On the running debate between Deakins and the Coens over their taste for wide-angle lenses.

clippings.speaker: Roger Deakins
clippings.quote: So Joel and Ethan had this small project up in Minnesota that they wanted to do, and they weren't sure if I would want to do it cause it was so low budget. I always remember that. I said, 'Well, you must be mad. Why wouldn't I want to do it?'
clippings.title: Oscar-winning cinematographer Roger Deakins on the funny reason he began working with Coens, 'disaster' of 'Shawshank' release and more
clippings.context: Deakins recalling how Fargo came to him after The Hudsucker Proxy flopped, in a career-retrospective interview.

clippings.speaker: Roger Deakins
clippings.quote: I remember Joel and Ethan saying, just a passing comment one day, … that they were gonna be writing a script of the novel No Country for Old Men. And the first thing I said was, 'Well, are you gonna direct it?' And they said, 'We don't know, really.' And I said, 'Dammit, I'll never talk to you again if you don't direct it and ask me to shoot it.'
clippings.title: Oscar-winning cinematographer Roger Deakins on the funny reason he began working with Coens, 'disaster' of 'Shawshank' release and more
clippings.context: Deakins on pushing the Coens to direct No Country for Old Men themselves.

clippings.speaker: Roger Deakins
clippings.quote: Obviously, with Joel and Ethan, I pretty much will do anything.
clippings.title: Roger Deakins
clippings.context: Deakins, interviewed by Jeff Bridges, on how he chooses projects.

clippings.speaker: Roger Deakins
clippings.quote: Joel and Ethan will do that sometimes. There will be storyboarding on a scene to have a lot of coverage, and we’ll go in in the morning and shoot, like, a two shot, and then I’ll say, “Well, we’ve got the overs now.” And they’ll say, “Well, I don’t think we need them.” … They’re also very confident when they feel they’ve got something.
clippings.title: Roger Deakins
clippings.context: Deakins, talking with Jeff Bridges, on the Coens' confidence on set.

notes: Joel rarely speaks about Deakins apart from Ethan; all Joel quotes come from the 1996 AC Fargo piece. Deakins's quotes address 'Joel and Ethan' jointly. Filmmaker Magazine returned 403.
